+            result = cursor.fetchone()
+        return result[0]

result.response:
I have resolved the issue in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-dl55t46t/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) in [compiler.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-dl55t46t/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py).

### Cause
When executing `Model.objects.all().delete()`, the underlying [`DeleteQuery`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-dl55t46t/django/db/models/sql/subqueries.py#L15-L44) did not have its initial base table alias populated in `alias_map` (or had a `0` refcount) prior to evaluating [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-dl55t46t/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412). As a result, `single_alias` evaluated to `False` (`0 == 1`), causing [`SQLDeleteCompiler.as_sql()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-dl55t46t/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1423-L1440) to fall back to the multi-table subquery deletion path (`DELETE FROM ... WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM ...)`).

### Fix
Call [`self.query.get_initial_alias()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-dl55t46t/django/db/models/sql/query.py#L916-L926) in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-dl55t46t/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) before counting active table aliases so the base table is always present and referenced in `alias_map`.
